steps.text: Rain and wind come hand in hand with evening in Kreis Sturmland. After generations of keepers, a house spire's decrepit stairwells will always hide moss somewhere in their cracks, no matter how the casters work to keep them clean.

He thinks of Zwillingstürme. Of the time when the black spire reminiscent of twisted horns had yet to be superseded by the newly erected twin spires, when the majestic city was called by a different name.

Of the dazzling auburn alleys in autumn, the kind he'd cross through in his youth, still sans wand or dagger. Nestled in his hands were but a few bound poetry collections, and precious hopes of freedom.

Not so anymore. Though the storm briefly abates, the spire's peak is still ruinously cold. Moonlight stabs through the drapery like rain, like a nail driven through each and every hope as it springs up.
What a shame, he laments.
Never again will he see the marigold in bloom.
Northern border of Leithanien, in Fels, the capital of Kreis Sturmland, 1100

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Marvelous, truly marvelous!

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: A performance of such fluency, as if the moonlight were caressing my cheeks—Herr Erich, what are your thoughts?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Martha, why do you treat me so?

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Why speak of her? It's not as if your ex-fiancée were here, Herr Erich.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The callousness in your features stings my heart deep, yet your beauty takes my breath away all the same. Such that I cannot forget—

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: I strongly suggest you move your hands away from my waist. People are watching.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: A-Apologies! Did the piece end already? I hadn't even realized.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I don't know why, but just now it was as if I'd been transported back to last autumn. To the day my Martha left me. The sorrow crushed my chest.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: As I always say, take more walks. Concerts like this may well be rare in Sturmland, but Zwillingstürme is a different story.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: *sigh* Sadly, I may not make it to Das Kaiserinnensfest this year.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: As I recall, meine Herr, you've a distant uncle with a seat at the Kurfürstenhof. Could it be you've heard something? I know that Kurfürst Werner—

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: No, nothing reliable at least.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: But the Kurfürst has hardly left his spire once these past months. Even the doctor rarely attends him anymore, while visits from casters serving other houses have only grown more frequent.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: It would seem almost none of us will be venturing outside of Sturmland these days. Das Kaiserinnensfest may come every year, but an audience with the new Lehnsherr? Who would dare miss that?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I wouldn't dream of it. No offense, but I'd prefer to spend my dreams with my lovely Martha instead.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Thank goodness we have Frau Arturia Giallo.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Only her cello can grant me a brief reprieve from the pressures of the day. A welcome breath of fresh air.

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Quite right. A pity that today will be her final concert here.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Then let me be drunk on it for a while more, just a while. After all, the storm is nigh again.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: What are you standing around for?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Did the steward not explain your duties? You're to return to the cellar immediately once dinner is served. Don't disturb the Kurfürst while he's resting.
The stern chastisement falls on deaf ears.
The servant walks off in a stupor. Down the steps and through the door, like a shell stripped of her soul, she ambles toward the cracking thunder outside.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Hold it.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Is that...

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: blood on your hands?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Is the Kurfürst...

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Guards, quickly!

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: *sigh* When will this weather make up its mind? If this keeps up, my firewood'll be damp again, and I just put it away.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Henk, could you start the fire already?! How long could it possibly take when the back garden is right there? Did you forget your wand again—
...May I have an extra candle, sir?

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Of course, Frau Droste. Will you be waiting here for someone again, like yesterday?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: The wind's especially strong tonight. You might want to go upstairs; it'll be warmer in there.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's fine. I haven't been back in so long, but... my body's still accustomed to the weather here.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Hahah, I just about forgot you're from Sturmland yourself.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: I saw an article about you in the paper a few years back, and I must say it caught me off guard. And here I thought I would recognize every young'un raised in these parts.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's not surprising you don't remember me. I'm just an ordinary person. I always have been.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Careful now, modesty kills.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: I even thought the article might've been poppycock until you strolled through the door of my shop. You have the poise and grace of a blueblood from up in the spires.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I appreciate what you've done for me over the last two days, Herr Müller. Especially...

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Don't you worry now, I won't tell a soul you're here. I know the media's been hounding you even after your retirement.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Look on the bright side. You're in Leithanien again: they only ever headline nobles and their big affairs.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...I suppose.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: But look at me, keeping you to myself again. Here's your candle. What else will you be needing?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Might you... have any more books you could lend me?

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: You got through that novel already? I'll check the cupboard, anything you'd like to read next? I've got... two illustrated guides, a historical fiction, and five or so poetry anthologies.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: I'm thinking you'd prefer the poems? Kurfürst Werner runs this folk poetry society, and all these poets like to turn up as special guests. Or so I hear.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: No, I'll have the historical fiction, please.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: After returning, I don't think I could stand any more poetry for a while.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Righty-o. Take this one, then, and don't worry about returning it anytime soon. I'll leave you be now.

steps.name: Grocer
steps.text: Henk, Henk—you little Lausbub, I know you're lazing about somewhere!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Die Glut. Embers...
It's an interesting tale. Though... it doesn't bear much resemblance to actual history.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ah, I didn't notice there were other customers. Guten Abend.
It certainly is a good evening.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: May I ask your name...?
Cora. Cora Löwenstein.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So I take it you've read this novel, Frau Löwenstein?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Regretfully, I've only been to the opera adapted from it. By the time it was published, I'd lost my ability to enjoy literature.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ah, your eyes... I apologize. That was tactless of me.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Oh, you get used to it after twenty or so years. Besides, it saves money on candles and firewood on nights like these. Do you mind if I sit a little nearer?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: What warm candleflame.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Did it start raining out there? Your clothes are damp.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I forgot to take my umbrella, what with the rush I was in.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Pardon me if I'm mistaken, but did you come here to meet me?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: All these years, and business here is still sluggish.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Or no, I suppose... everything in Sturmland is the same as ever. We're far from the capital, Catastrophes keep coming, and the weather here lives up to its name. Outside of special occasions, we hardly ever see many out-of-towners.

spans.text: in Sturmland is the same as ever. We're far from the capital, Catastrophes keep coming, and the weather here lives up to its name. Outside of special occasions, we hardly ever see many out-of-towners.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I still remember the view from this spot by the window. You can see the nomadic plate with the Kurfürst's parlor spire, can't you? He should've picked somewhere more out of the way for you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So it was him who sent you...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Hold my hand. Tight.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Listen closely.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I hear people... many of them, hiding outside in the gales.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You can control the candleflame by your hand, right Viviana?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I can.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Then on my mark, please—

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Let's 'extinguish.'
The instant the candlelight dims, the grocer's windows shatter into pieces.
The rainstorm outside pours in alongside assorted Arts energy covering a full spectrum of effects.
Viviana grips Cora's hand, struck with the sense that she's sitting on a skiff in the heart of a raging sea.
Wave after wave of Arts crash down on them, all but blowing the humble storefront to smithereens, yet precisely parting to leave the two of them unscathed.
Footsteps clack within the shop.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They can't tell where we are; they have to approach to feel us out. Can you sense their positions?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Crystal clear. Let me handle this.
Candleflame leaps anew from Viviana's palm.
The shadows come to life, reaching their limbs through the ruins and spreading across the rubble to pin the looming casters in place.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...Seven, eight.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Nine.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: We're safe for now.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You saved my life.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You handled the brunt of it. All I did was 'tune' their Arts a little.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Now, let's get away from here before more assassins come calling.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Who were they?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: People here to meet you, like me.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Will Herr Müller and Henk be in danger?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Our old gentleman's in the back garden—he avoided this attack. My colleague will get him to safety shortly.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: As for Herr Assistent... he's the one who called them. He should've known that dealing in shady business like this would earn him more than a handful of Originium ingots.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I... honestly don't see how I'm any sort of worthwhile target.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'll explain in a moment. For the time being, Viviana...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Could you let me take a proper 'look' at you?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You mean...
The woman's beautiful face may be unfamiliar to her, but her voice and expression are anything but. Viviana finds herself unable to decline.

Cora lifts her hands, and feels about for Viviana's cheeks, her fingers tracing a few soft strokes once they alight. Her movements are infinitely tender, the sort one would use for handling the most precious instrument.
And as if in response, tears well up in her lusterless eyes.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You resemble your mother so much.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: If only Werner could see you now, how joyous he would've been. So close, too... He spent so long struggling in his sickbed, just to see you one last time.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Werner... My father?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Did he...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm so sorry, Viviana.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Not long ago, your father... Sturmland-Kurfürst Werner... passed away in his spire.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: And that was how it transpired, meine Herr. We were all in our places keeping watch. Nobody expected the assassin to infiltrate the Kurfürst's room.
The assassin. You mean to say, the Kurfürst's personal attendant?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Ja, meine Herr.
She had been employed in this spire for more than half her life.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: The Kurfürst trusted her implicitly, as did we all. Yet without a doubt, she was the last to see him alive.
Did anyone else enter the room after the incident?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Only the personal bodyguard and the doctor.
Did anyone at all step outside?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Nein, not one of us set foot outside the parlor spire this evening.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: We still haven't identified who among us is to blame, so we've locked all the servants in the basement cells for now. Shall I show you the way?
No need. I've already met with them.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Did you question the assassin?
Having been under the effects of psychological Arts, she has no recollection of her whereabouts.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: We should try torturing her. Otherwise, it's near-impossible to determine if she's lying.
Well then. Are you lying?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Me? Nein, meine Herr, how could I? I've been loyal to the Hochberg family for over a decade! Everything I have I owe to Kurfürst Werner!
Then... would you swear that upon the Güldenesgesatz?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: Güldenesgesatz... The Golden Movement...

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: H-How would I dare deceive a Gesatzswächter!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You left the spire after what happened in there.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You have the smell of rainwater on you. The hem of your clothes has brushed against the moss in the cracks of the steps outside.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Ten years is nothing. You don't yet know House Hochberg's spire well enough, just as you didn't know Kurfürst Werner well enough.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: The Kurfürst... He summoned you here...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Kurfürst picked up on your disloyalty. You began stirring into action once he fell ill.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: I only regret that Frau Löwenstein and I were ultimately one step behind.

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Send notice to the Concertmaster that the Gesatzswächter's found that—

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Earrgh—!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It is futile to resist the melody's fetters. Much like your wisdom, your Arts are ugly and brittle.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Where did you send that thing?

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Gakhakha—ggh!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Answer me, remnant.

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Z... Zwillingstü...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Is your 'Concertmaster' the one who used psychological Arts to influence the attendant? Are they also in Zwillingstürme?

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: The Concert... master...

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: No, my head... MY HEAD!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The Golden Melody now resounds in the deepest parts of your soul.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Any intent to disobey, and your mind will collapse beneath its weight.

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Gesatzswächter...

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: With such absolute power, why must you serve as a thrall to the Twin Puppets?!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It is not my melody that restrains you, nor the decree of the Kaiserinnen.

spans.text: melody that restrains you, nor the decree of the Kaiserinnen.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: What you are failing to resist is the will of Leithanien herself.

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: The will of... Leithanien?

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: Hah... hahah! Since when did the present-day Leithanien... have even a fraction of the will she should?

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: The Genesis Horn... The might of the great Herkunftshorn will come to enshroud this land anew!

steps.name: 'Spire Caster'
steps.text: GKHAAAAAAAAGHH!

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The feeble sound that death plays. A caster that can seize such cries over such a long distance is no ordinary remnant.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...The Concertmaster.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Frau, the ride for Zwillingstürme is here. Are we leaving right now?
Yes. Let's go.
The friend who invited me here has just taken the curtain call. I've played every piece I needed to.
There's no reason to linger here any longer.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Somehow, without realizing... I'd been staying here all this time...

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Martha, my dear Martha... Oh, it's like I'm dreaming. How long would I have to wait to hear such a remarkable performance again?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I've told you people, you are not to disturb me whenever I'm attending a con—

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: What? Wait, what did you say?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I'll be back posthaste. Get my ride ready. I need to see a few friends.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: And one more thing—I want the wood carving I bought in Kreis Lupukarn, as well as the Victorian porcelain I keep in the study. Bring them both.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Why such haste? Was the Kurfürst not alive and well this morning?

spans.text: Why such haste? Was the Kurfürst not alive and well this morning?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The days to come will be arduous once more. Oh, Arturia... Only your music and your beauty can deliver me from this nightmare.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The sheer effort I went to just to arrive at her interim abode, only to find she'd already...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please continue.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: C-Continue? Who are you? And what's that you're holding? A wand or a—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You mentioned an intent to visit Arturia. I assume you have some relation to her.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am currently searching for her. Therefore, I require any and all pertinent leads.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: You're looking for Frau Giallo too? Are you some fanatic follower of hers?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Follower? That is a highly inaccurate description.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Per the tenets of the law, and on special assignment by the Curia, I must apprehend the fugitive and repatriate her to Laterano.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: F-Fugitive? Frau Giallo is a guest of the Kurfürst, and no matter the rumors from outside... No, I find you far more suspicious!

spans.text: F-Fugitive? Frau Giallo is a guest of the Kurfürst, and no matter the rumors from outside... No, I find

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: Herr Erich! Are you still well?

steps.name: Older Noble
steps.text: They put the alley under lockdown out there; Gendarmerie all over. I hear even a Gesatzswächter went over to the Kurfürst's parlor spire.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Danke, I'm well enough. I was just about to visit a few Grafen and see what word I could pick off the grapevine. *sigh* How uncanny can one night get? Damn my indolent chauffeur—where is he?!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: At least one small stroke of fortune is that Frau Giallo has already safely departed for Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Wait, where did that eerie Sankta get off to?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...The fugitive Arturia is no longer here.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Executor Federico, continuing pursuit of target.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Destination: Zwillingstürme, capital of Leithanien.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It's time we got going too, Viviana.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They'll announce that the Kurfürst passed from illness. It's understandable. A white lie to keep the domain in order.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I won't be able to attend the funeral, will I?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I'm so sorry. You never even got to see him one last time after you rushed back from Kazimierz and everything. And now you can't even go to...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Mourn him.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm not even sure I have the right to anyway.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I scarcely remember how he looked. In all these years, all the word 'father' meant to me was just the letters he sent to Kazimierz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And yet I can't help but think that even the letters themselves might well have been written by a retainer in his stead.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Your father never once forgot about you.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Mm... So everyone tells me, including himself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And I'm willing to believe it.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But as I read that last letter, I still hesitated. I didn't know if I should... No, if I wanted to come back.

spans.text: But as I read that last letter, I still hesitated. I didn't know if I should... No, if I

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You have a tender heart, Viviana. I can't imagine you'd ever decline a dying man's last wish.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Or perhaps... it was the spire I wanted to see one last time.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Just to see if it still towered over the clouds, like I remembered.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You can't go back there. At least, not for now.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: For your own safety, we shouldn't remain in Sturmland for long.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Were the ones who took his life and the casters who came for me last night... sent by the same people?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Not necessarily. With Werner gone, anyone that knows who you are has reason enough to make a move against you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: You're your father's sole descendant. In times this turbulent, neither his enemies, nor his former vassals, nor anyone else potentially in line to succeed him will just leave you be.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Then what about you? Why are you protecting me?

spans.text: Then what about you? Why are

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Think, and you might still recall, child. Thirteen years ago, upon your mother's passing, I was the one who took you to the Grand Knight Territory.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Then you're... the Imperial Orchestra of Leithanien's...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Instrument tuner. Quite a convenient role.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: The Reichsorchester's visit symbolized the friendly ties between Leithanien and Kazimierz. No one would think to question a child with an instrument among them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: So you've saved my life... more than once.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It was your father who wanted to, more than anyone.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Some months ago, Werner realized his days were waning, and he worried that after he left us, you'd be dragged down as a sacrifice in the power struggle.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Your role in this is unique. Whether you chose to return to Leithanien or stay in Kazimierz, the waves would have reached you regardless.

spans.text: Whether you chose to return to Leithanien or stay in Kazimierz, the waves would have reached you regardless.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: He had no choice but to turn to me and Brandt. He hoped that as old friends of his, we could bring you safely to Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: There, you'll be under the protection of the Kaiserinnen.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Protection... of the Empresses?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Ja. That's what Werner wanted for you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Viviana von Hochberg—

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: In the name of your family, you are to serve as an Empresses' Voice.
Central Leithanien, Kreis Einwald, in a town on the outskirts of Zwillingstürme, not far from the city gate

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: *huff*... *pant*... I need sleep. Verdammt! Why am I on duty again?

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Those spry young wretches, always clocking out early. What excuse did they have today, a new movie? Some underground live show?

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: The moment the month rolls over, I'll see that I get a word in with the Baron, to speed up my transfer to Zwillingstürme...

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Hey, you there!

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: What are you doing, loitering here this late?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I am taking my regular walk.

spans.text: I am taking my regular walk.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: To my knowledge, there have been no new decrees forbidding law-abiding citizens like myself from rambling the wilds past midnight.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: ...Well, you're not wrong.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Just another bored youth going for a walk. Why was I getting so nervous?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Am I free to go now? I appreciate your concern.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Go on, be on your— Wait.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Why do I get the feeling... I've seen you somewhere before?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You could be mistaken. After all, you did just tell me that strolling nighttime youths are as common as anything.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Where are you from? By your accent, I'm guessing the Urtica Grafschaft?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I was born there... in the countryside.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Countryside? What kind of country bumpkin talks like that? Stop being ridiculous.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: No... Now that you mention it, I've never heard any commoner pronounce things the way you do. Say, you wouldn't happen to be the runaway son of some small-time noble, would you?

spans.text: No... Now that you mention it, I've never heard
commoner pronounce things the way you do. Say, you wouldn't happen to be the runaway son of some small-time noble, would you?

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Let me check your ID.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If you're fantasizing about gaining the favor of some aristocrat for returning me, then you will be sorely disappointed.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: ...Has anyone ever told you that the way you talk could seriously piss people off?

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: ID. Now.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Pardon, pardon, I've got my boy's passport right here. Do peruse.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: And who are you?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Come on, you don't remember me? I live in the city. That second-hand bookshop guy.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Speaking of which, the books aren't quite flying off the shelves, and lately I've been thinking, what about a cafe instead? You must be awfully tired this late on patrol, no? Here, here, try my coffee. My own brew.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: *choke*... Mein Gott, the taste... I'd forget about that cafe if I were you, for your own sake.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Haha, as long as it wakes you up. So are you done with the passport?

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: ...Ebenholz. That's your full name?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: His parents just love the piano. The keys, especially—it was between Ebenholz or Elfenbein.

spans.text: the piano. The keys, especially—it was between Ebenholz or Elfenbein.

steps.name: Tired Security Guard
steps.text: Well, whatever, be on your way. You think they pay me enough to question a kid's legal name? And yes, give me all the disgusting swill you've got left, I'll need it.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: If you'd known you'd be back so soon, would you have not burned your passport?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I regret nothing.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If you must know, I naturally assumed that whenever you people wanted me back, you'd simply print a second one. Or as many as you need.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: ...So why did you come back?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: For the hundreds of thousands of residents of the Urtica Grafschaft. Over a hundred retainers in the spire alone. I'm not so far gone in my selfishness that I'd sacrifice them all for my so-called freedom.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Which means you can stop it with the jokes, my dear spy. Or did Their Majesties send you to try me again? See if maybe I'll pour my heart out and wait on them hand and foot?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: With Das Kaiserinnensfest approaching, Zwillingstürme has been restless lately.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Heh... And of course I still have that thing in my head.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I know better than any of you that the performance of this ludicrously grating piece is far from over.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Listen to me, meine Herr. My mission ends here.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Once you head into Zwillingstürme, someone else will pick you up.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Maybe you've already realized this, but you had two correspondence. One ordering you to come to the capital, and the other granting you your official 'death.' But it wasn't the same Majesty that wrote both.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Compared to the first's benevolence, the other...
Ebenholz doesn't even let Biegler finish before walking off.
Just before disappearing around the corner for good, the young man waves ta-ta to him.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: So you knew.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: Former Graf Urtica, are you hoping for... a true death this time?

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: *huff*... I'm getting sentimental now, in all this miserable gray weather.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: May you...

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: No, never mind.

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: If people like us still have a shred of luck to spare—

steps.name: Biegler
steps.text: —Then let's pray we never have to meet again.
